title: 2020-08 — TEs Gendall, Hightower & Lien v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the 2020-08 complaint and answered it by reference to its decision in Case No. 2020-07. That incorporated decision sustained Wilbourne's complaint, annulled his deposition, and recommended treating his 17-month suspension as sufficient definite suspension. No separate merits analysis or independent censure annulment was issued for 2020-08.
first_summary: The SJC sustained the complaint of TEs Gendall, Hightower, and Lien against Pacific Presbytery. The complaint alleged that Presbytery mishandled a BCO 38-1 confession by TE Rankin Wilbourne, including by allowing a prejudicial Judicial Commission report before the agreed statement of facts. The SJC answered the 2020-08 complaint by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07, which sustained Wilbourne's complaint and annulled his deposition.
summary: The SJC sustained the complaint of TEs Gendall, Hightower, and Lien against Pacific Presbytery's handling of a BCO 38-1 confession by TE Rankin Wilbourne. Presbytery had denied the complaint. The SJC held that reading a prejudicial six-page judicial-commission report before the agreed statement of facts violated BCO 38-1 and tainted the censure. It answered the 2020-08 complaint by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07, which annulled Wilbourne's deposition and recommended treating his 17-month suspension as sufficient definite suspension.

sources.supports: Identity and caption: combined 2020-07/2020-08/2020-09 matter; Case 2020-08 is identified as TEs Gendall, Hightower & Lien.
Dispute: 2020-08 complaint grounds and Presbytery's denial.
Outcome: issue framed; SJC sustained and answered 2020-08 by reference to 2020-07; roll-call adoption.
Incorporated relief: Case 2020-07 sustained, deposition annulled, 17-month suspension treated as definite suspension, matter recommended closed.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source is a combined decision for Cases 2020-07, 2020-08, and 2020-09 (line 1). Case 2020-08 is identified at line 192 as TEs Gendall, Hightower & Lien. The Panel decision was drafted by RE Howie Donahoe, amended and unanimously approved by the Panel, further amended by the full SJC, and adopted 19-0-0 (lines 369–373).
evidence_notes.dispute: The 2020-08 complaint alleged six constitutional concerns about Pacific Presbytery's BCO 38-1 process, including BCO 40-4, 38-1, 34-7, 32-20, 27-5 & 31-5, and 31-8 (lines 156–178). Presbytery denied the complaint 13-21 on July 18, 2020 (line 182), and the complainants carried it to the SJC on August 4, 2020 (line 184).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC asked whether Presbytery clearly erred in handling a BCO 38-1 case without process and in the prior BCO 31-2 investigation (lines 212–214). It held yes because the six-page Judicial Commission report contained new and prejudicial assertions beyond the agreed statement, violating BCO 38-1 (lines 220–241). The operative final line states that the 2020-08 complaint is sustained and answered by reference to the decision (line 367).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The detailed merits discussion and censure relief are expressly framed for Case 2020-07; 2020-08 is disposed by reference. The SJC did not separately re-annul a censure in 2020-08. The roll call shows several absent members and one disqualification, with the decision approved 19-0-0 (lines 371–373).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Case 2020-07 is incorporated by reference within the same source: the SJC sustained Wilbourne's complaint, annulled the deposition, recommended treating the past 17-month suspension as definite suspension, stated no further censure or indictment was recommended, and recommended Presbytery consider the matter closed (lines 218, 242–262, 367).

source_limits: The source is a combined three-complaint decision. Case 2020-08's own complaint is summarized but not separately argued in the reasoning; the SJC applies the 2020-07 analysis by reference. The synopsis therefore treats the 2020-07 censure relief as incorporated by reference and does not infer separate rulings on each of the six 2020-08 constitutional concerns. The source heading at line 13 names only Case 2020-09, while Case 2020-08 appears at line 192 and is disposed at line 367.

score_reasons.distinctive_value: Captures the useful rule that a BCO 38-1 court should see only the agreed statement before censure, plus the by-reference disposition.
